decision.argument_basis: scope evidence not reflected in the mapping
decision.evidence_cited: Employee has personally unblocked sign-off on 6 of the last 8 difficult closure escalations company-wide over 11 years -- this is company-wide, cross-tapeout, cross-team final technical authority on analog closure, not scope confined to a single team or product line. Section 4's Distinguished MTS anchor describes exactly this pattern: 'the person other Principal MTS engineers escalate to,' with 'final technical sign-off authority within the domain' spanning the roadmap rather than one product. The absence of patents or publications does not undercut this -- Section 6 is explicit that the Fellow honorific (and by extension external recognition) is a separate, optional track-record marker, not a component of the level anchor itself; Distinguished MTS's anchor requires only that decisions 'shape how Nyx builds silicon for years,' which is what company-wide closure escalation authority reflects.
decision.framework_section: Section 4 (Level anchors, Distinguished MTS row) and Section 6 (Fellow)
